COMMUNITY / HELP & SUPPORT

A little context.
A better answer.

Bring a small, reproducible example. Keep private captures out of public issues.

Questions and reproducible bug reports live in the public community repository. You do not need access to the private research repository to read the documentation or contribute a synthetic reproduction.

Something broke?

Use the bug template for unexpected package behavior. Include a minimal synthetic trace, expected and actual behavior, and your environment.

Report a reproducible bug ↗

Finding your way?

Use the question template for integration and usage help. Start with the artifact-delivery quickstart and share the smallest example that explains your question.

Ask a question ↗

A useful report includes

  • Consequa-X version, Python version and operating system.
  • Reproduction steps and the smallest synthetic input.
  • The expected result and the actual error or conclusion.
  • Relevant sanitized output, with no customer or production data.

Keep private evidence private.

Public issues require a GitHub account and are visible to everyone. Do not post credentials, exploit details, private traces or identifying customer data. Minimal-disclosure HTML still retains timing, counts and relationships; review it before sharing. Use a synthetic reproduction whenever possible.

Suspected vulnerabilities belong in private vulnerability reporting, rather than a public issue. Maintainer help is best effort; no response deadline or long-term support period is promised.

Source and distribution

The research/source repository is private. The public community repository contains documentation, synthetic examples and issue templates. The MIT-licensed Python wheel and source distribution are public; the source distribution includes implementation, application examples, tests and documentation.
